### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, activities A14, A15 and A16 each occurred in about 35%, 30% and 35% of traces, never together, and each was followed by A24. In the later window, these three activities are absent (0% participation). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL008, REL006, REL012, REL017]
- In the earlier window, A21, A22 and A23 were absent; in the later window, each occurs in every trace (100% participation). [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- In the earlier window, A39 led to A14, A15 and A16 (about 35%, 30% and 35% of its outgoing transitions). In the later window, A39 leads to A21, A22 and A23 (about 36%, 33% and 32%). [DIR007]
- In the later window, A21, A22 and A23 co-occur in every trace and appear in both orders with similar frequency (about 51% vs 49% for each pair), so there is no fixed order among them. [REL019, REL020, REL023]
- In the later window, A21, A22 and A23 each precede A24, and A39 precedes each of them. [REL021, REL022, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027]
- A24 remains present in all traces in both windows, but its position shifts later: mean relative position from about 0.39 to 0.44, and the lag from A39 to A24 changes from 2 steps to 4 steps. [POS007, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change from a choice among three alternative activities (A14, A15, A16) after A39 to a sequence of three activities (A21, A22, A23) that are all executed, in any order, before A24. The earlier window shows exactly one of A14/A15/A16 per trace (never co-occurring) and each leading to A24; the later window shows all three of A21/A22/A23 in every trace, co-occurring with no fixed order, and each leading to A24. A39's outgoing edges switch from the old set to the new set. A24 is still the final activity but occurs later, consistent with the added activities. The evidence is direct and consistent across occurrence, direction, relation, position and lag indicators. A competing explanation that the old activities were simply renamed is unlikely because the new activities co-occur with each other while the old ones were mutually exclusive, and the order among the new ones is not fixed. The main limitation is that we cannot rule out that the new activities are a different representation of the same underlying work, but the behavioural change in structure is clear.
